summary: Each of the 40 genes in the published hypothalamus Table 1B has a unique registered SHAM ozone-versus-air effect, and all agree in direction. Pearson is 0.976 and Spearman is 0.885, so the selected list meets only the directional criterion of author-concordance-v2. The full author results and numeric per-gene P values and FDR remain unavailable.

manualReview.summary: All 40 published hypothalamus Table 1B genes agree in direction
manualReview.note: The GEO matrix and family SOFT match their pinned hashes. Four ozone and four air SHAM hypothalamus BioSamples match the registered sample sheet. The authors report SHAM ozone/air fold changes from an analysis using DESeq2 on rounded counts. We took log2 of each published ratio, including ratios below one. The registered limma coefficient is mean log2(normalized count + 1) in ozone minus the corresponding air mean. Pearson is 0.97595 and Spearman is 0.88509. The directional route of author-concordance-v2 passes for the selected genes. The correlation route falls below its Spearman cutoff. The authors selected the most increased and decreased significant genes for Table 1B. They report a study-wide FDR cutoff but give no numeric P or adjusted P for individual rows.
reviewFlags: Table 1B contains a selected, rounded effect list. Gene-level numerical inference and the complete tested universe remain unassessed.

verificationReview.reason: Original-author Table 1B is available and compared. No complete SHAM hypothalamus ozone-versus-air gene result was located in the sources documented in SEARCH_LOG.md. Pearson is 0.97595 and Spearman is 0.88509. The directional route of author-concordance-v2 passes for the selected genes. The correlation route falls below its Spearman cutoff. DESeq2 and limma estimate the group change differently.
verificationReview.nextStep: For full-universe comparison, obtain the original SHAM hypothalamus ozone-versus-air DESeq2 output for all tested genes, with identifiers, unrounded effects, raw and adjusted P, model design, coefficient settings and filtering.

comparabilityReview.basis: Published Table 1B log2 fold changes against the registered limma coefficients. All authors' rows in the hypothalamus panel were retained.
comparabilityReview.reference: Henriquez et al., Toxicological Sciences, DOI 10.1093/toxsci/kfz182, Table 1B and supplementary methods. The publisher's final table resolves spacing and numeric-cell artifacts in PMC9344225. GSE133293 supplies the normalized counts and sample metadata.

cohort.note: The original study sampled whole hypothalamus from male Wistar-Kyoto rats. The four air and four ozone SHAM samples (GSM3905188–GSM3905195) each have a distinct BioSample, registered expression column and matching ENA run. The reported tissue comparison excludes brainstem and AD arms.

contrast.note: Table 1B labels SH O3 / SH air. Ozone exposure was 0.8 ppm for four hours, with filtered air as the baseline. The registered groupcase coefficient has the same numerator and denominator.

features.note: Exact case-sensitive published rat symbols join uniquely for 40/40 selected rows. No aliases, ambiguous joins or unmatched selected rows. Whole-universe identifier and filtering coverage remains unknown.

effects.note: The authors report SHAM ozone/air fold changes from an analysis using DESeq2 on rounded counts. We took log2 of each published ratio, including ratios below one. The registered limma coefficient is mean log2(normalized count + 1) in ozone minus the corresponding air mean. Both quantify the same direction on a log2 scale. The source ratios are rounded to two decimal places. Pearson is 0.97595 and Spearman is 0.88509. The directional route of author-concordance-v2 passes for the selected genes. The correlation route falls below its Spearman cutoff. Median absolute log2 difference is 0.24700, maximum 1.86760 for Hif3a, and the registered-to-author RMS ratio is 1.39909.

inference.note: The authors used DESeq2 1.10.1 and included rows at FDR ≤ 0.10. They report 311 increased and 257 decreased hypothalamus genes. Registered limma gives 170 calls at the same cutoff, including 38 Table 1B genes. At registered FDR < 0.05 the counts are 66 overall and 26 on Table 1B. All 66 local discoveries lack a numeric author FDR, including 40 without a Table 1B row. Author calls at 0.05, exact per-gene P/FDR agreement and whole positive-list overlap are unassessed.

coverage.note: The paired list covers 40/40 author-selected genes and 40/20,845 registered genes (0.192%). The remaining 20,805 registered effects and the 528 other author discoveries have no paired Table 1B coefficient.

comparabilityReview.criteria: Use every Table 1B gene. The selected reference is the coverage denominator. Author-concordance-v2 requires compatible cohort, contrast, identifiers and effect definitions, ≥30 paired genes and ≥90% coverage, plus either Pearson and Spearman both ≥0.90, or ≥90% same-gene sign agreement among ≥30 nonzero pairs covering ≥90% of pairs. Magnitude and inference are contextual.
comparabilityReview.conclusion: 40 of 40 nonzero pairs agree in direction. Pearson is 0.97595 and Spearman is 0.88509. The directional route of author-concordance-v2 passes for the selected genes. The correlation route falls below its Spearman cutoff. The table provides selected-gene effect evidence only. Whole-universe inference and full verification remain open.

openIssues: The full original-author result and fitted DESeq2 design, filtering and coefficient settings are needed to reconcile genome-wide effects and inference.
